newsitem.title: UK: Tanker chartering rates mostly steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tanker chartering rates mostly steady to firmer.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering rates were mostly steady to firmer on Tuesday, with moderate activity seen out of West Africa, across the Mediterranean, in Asia/Pacific and Western hemisphere, brokers said.

Tight modern tonnage space saw rates for shipments from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf firming with one million barrels booked transatlantic at W97.5, up around 12 points in the afternoon after the market showed a slight softer tone initially.
Mediterranean rates were slightly softer despite fairly active trade. Brokers reported sufficient older tonnage around to meet current cross-Mediterranean demand.
Good Aframax activity was seen from North Africa and the Black Sea. North African rates slipped a couple of points to trade around W100 but Black Sea routes held around W102.5
In the Mideast Gulf/Red Sea region Asian charterers continued to dominate. One vessel was reported booked to the West but no rate for the cargo was reported.
Shipping brokers said rates out of the Middle East Gulf on VLCCs to Japan were steady around W62.5, the last traded level, but no vessels were seen booked today.
South Korea and Singapore levels were steady, with Hyundai seen fixing a VLCC to South Korea at W55.
New fixings in the Asia/Pacific region featured mostly Aframax tonnage. Many vessels were done at fixed price levels with USAC fixtures taking around $1.2-$1.3 million.
In the U.K./continent Aframaxes continued to find employment but rates slipped 2.5 points with early trade at W102.50 for a vessel fixed from Flotta/UKC.
The Caribbean market was slightly firmer in active trade with 70,000 tonners accepting W132.50, up 2.50 points.
